summary: Tested the new Live API Latency Speedometer feature end-to-end. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests passed covering endpoint shape, middleware capture, path normalisation (/patients/pat_abc123456789 collapses to :id), RBAC 403 for non-founder, auth-required, and regression on /system/health, /system/data-health, /dashboard. Frontend: LatencySpeedometer renders on /admin/dashboard with all required data-testids (latency-card, latency-gauge, latency-p95-value, latency-health-pill='Healthy', lat-p50/p95/p99/rps/count5m/uptime, latency-slowest-table). Numbers populated with live data (p95=5ms, 374 reqs in 5m, gauge needle drawn). 5s polling verified indirectly via networkidle timeout (page never goes idle because widget keeps re-fetching).
critical_code_review_comments: utils/latency_recorder.py::_normalise_path — the >12-char rule collapses legitimate route segments too (e.g. /api/subscriptions → 'subscriptions' is 13 chars → ':id'). Consider length threshold >20 or a stricter id-shape regex to keep readable paths in the slowest-routes table.

LatencyRecorderMiddleware runs even on 401/403 auth-rejected requests which is correct, but path is normalised BEFORE routing — parameters like ?token=... aren't stripped from raw_path only because url.path excludes query. Fine, just noting.
Per-worker buffer is documented; when scaling to multiple uvicorn workers the numbers become per-worker. OK for now.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Latency middleware buffer is per-worker & in-memory — restarting backend clears it. If pytest count assertion fails, verify supervisor hasn't restarted backend between test runs. Audiologist user is on clinic-pytest-suite tenant, so the 403 comes from the PLATFORM_CLINIC_ID fence in require_permission (before permission check) — which is the correct behaviour.
